description.p: Provides all mandatory features from the XSLT 3.0 specification (including try/catch, iterate, accumulators, maps, named modes, content value templates, and extended patterns, as well as features retained from XSLT 2.0).

Provides a schema-aware XSLT 3.0 processor: specifically, the ability to import an XSD schema when compiling a stylesheet, to use this for type-checking, and to process and create schema-validated instance documents.

Provides the serialization feature: specifically, the ability to convert the result trees produced as output of an XSLT transformation to lexical XML, or other formats including HTML, JSON, and plain text, under the control of serialization parameters defined in the stylesheet or via an external API.

Provides XSLT 1.0 compatibility mode as defined in the XSLT 3.0 specification. If a stylesheet specifies version="1.0", this causes certain constructs to behave in a way that retains the XSLT 1.0 behavior.
Includes additional features of the XSLT 3.0 specification that enable streaming (processing of documents that are too large to fit in memory).
Provides use of the XSLT 3.0 instruction xsl:evaluate, which allows dynamic evaluation of XPath expressions.
Provides full use of XPath 3.1 features, including XPath 3.1 functions, and maps and arrays.

p.i: Note: Saxon supports XPath 3.1 unconditionally in XSLT 3.0 stylesheets, it does not offer a processing mode in which XPath is restricted to version 3.0.

description.p: Provides higher-order functions: specifically, the ability to use functions as values, including dynamic function calls, inline functions, partial function application, and the standard higher-order functions defined in the XPath 3.1 function library.

Provides all XPath 3.1 features which do not require schema-awareness or higher-order functions. This includes an implementation of maps and arrays, and support for JSON, as well as language constructs retained from earlier XPath versions.

Provides schema-awareness: specifically, any use of source documents with type annotations, and any use of XPath expressions that contain the names of schema components such as element declarations and types, other than the built-in types.

Provides higher-order functions: specifically, the ability to use functions as values, including dynamic function calls, inline functions, partial function application, and a library of built-in higher-order functions.
Provides Minimal Conformance (including try/catch and "group-by", as well as language features retained from earlier XQuery versions) as defined in section 5 of the XQuery 3.1 specification.
Provides the Schema Aware feature. This enables a query to import an XSD schema and use it for type checking, and to validate instance documents.
Provides the Typed Data feature. This enables a query to accept input data that has been validated against a schema.
Saxon does not implement the Static Typing feature.

p.i: The static typing feature treats an expression as an error unless it is guaranteed type-safe at compile time. Without this feature, type checking is performed dynamically at run time. Saxon does compile time analysis to minimize the amount of dynamic checking that is needed.

description.p: Provides the Module feature, which allows a query to be made up of multiple modules.

Provides the Serialization feature. This allows the output of a query to be serialized as lexical XML, or in other formats including HTML, JSON, and plain text, under the control of serialization parameters contained either in the query itself, or supplied externally.

Provides the Higher-Order Function feature. This provides the ability to use functions as values, including dynamic function calls, inline functions, partial function application, and a library of built-in higher-order functions.
Saxon provides all the features defined in the XQuery Update 1.0 specification. The implementation allows XQuery Update 1.0 syntax to be mixed with XQuery 3.1 syntax.

p.i: XQuery Update in SaxonCS is offered "as is": the feature is present, but has not been extensively tested.

description.p: Saxon includes a complete implementation of XML Schema 1.0. This provides the ability to process XSD 1.0 schema documents and use them to validate instance documents. Note that Saxon does not expose the full PSVI, as required by the conformance rules in the XSD 1.0 Recommendation. Also includes Saxon extension functions to provide access to a compiled schema.

p.i: From Saxon 10, the Saxon schema processor accepts XSD 1.1 syntax unconditionally. XSD 1.0 schemas are processed according to the rules of the XSD 1.1 specification. This offers a very high level of backwards compatibility, except in a few areas where the XSD 1.0 rules were unclear and have been clarified in the XSD 1.1 recommendation.

description.p: Saxon includes a complete implementation of XML Schema 1.1. This provides the ability to process schema documents that use the new features of XSD 1.1, and use them to validate instance documents. More specifically, in the language of section 2.4 of the specification, it is a General-Purpose Web-Aware Validator. Also includes Saxon extension functions to provide access to a compiled schema.
Allows hot-spot code generation for XSLT, XQuery, XPath, and XML Schema, typically giving a 25% performance boost.

This feature performs static analysis of a query and uses this to filter a document during loading, so that the only parts held in memory are those parts needed to answer the query. For simple queries on large documents this can give substantial memory savings.

XSLT 3.0 packaging allows stylesheet modules to be independently compiled and distributed, and provides much more "software engineering" control over public and private interfaces, and the like. The ability to save packages in compiled form ("stylesheet export file", SEF) gives much faster loading of frequently used stylesheets, and also enables in-browser execution using SaxonJS.
Allows the importing of stylesheet packages in compiled form. Possible with all editions provided the package only uses features available in that edition.

alt-description.p: Allows the importing of stylesheet packages in compiled form. Possible with all editions provided the package only uses features available in that edition. Note that this edition does not provide the ability to create compiled stylesheet packages.

description.p: Takes advantage of multi-core CPUs by providing automatic parallel execution of the collection() function.

Takes advantage of multi-core CPUs by providing automatic parallel execution of the xsl:result-document instruction; plus an extension attribute saxon:threads to allow multi-threaded execution of xsl:for-each instructions under the control of the stylesheet author.

The Basic optimizer provided with all Saxon editions provides a wide range of static and dynamic optimizations including full pipelining of sequence operations, lazy evaluation of variables, elimination of redundant sorting operations, etc. The Advanced optimizer additionally provides join optimization and inlining of variables and functions, where feasible.

The Basic optimizer provided with all Saxon editions provides a wide range of static and dynamic optimizations including full pipelining of list operations, lazy evaluation of variables, elimination of redundant sorting operations, etc.

The Advanced optimizer provides the wide range of static and dynamic optimizations featured in the Basic optimizer - including full pipelining of list operations, lazy evaluation of variables, elimination of redundant sorting operations, etc. - and additionally provides join optimization, inlining of variables and functions, just-in-time compilation of template rules, and optimized searching of large sets of template rules, where feasible.

The W3C web server routinely rejects requests for commonly-referenced files such as the DTD for XHTML, causing parsing failures. In response to this, Saxon now includes copies of these documents within the issued JAR/DLL file, and recognizes requests for these documents, satisfying the request using the local copy.
Provides saxon:stream(), an extension function to allow large documents to be processed without holding the whole document in memory.
Allows large documents to be processed without holding the whole document in memory. Provides the streaming features of the XSLT 3.0 specification.
A selection of EXSLT extension functions are provided (in the modules Common, Dates and Times, Math, Random, and Sets), as listed in the documentation.
Only the exslt:node-set function is available in SaxonCS.

alt-description.p: A selection of EXSLT extension functions are provided (in the modules Common, Dates and Times, Math, Random, and Sets), as listed in the documentation.

description.p: A selection of EXPath extension functions are provided (in the modules Archive, Binary, and File), as listed in the documentation.
Ability to write extension functions (for use in XSLT, XQuery, or XPath) by implementing a Saxon-defined interface and registering the implementation with the Saxon Configuration.
Ability to access existing Java methods dynamically and invoke them as extension functions by means of dynamic loading and reflexion.
Ability to access existing JavaScript objects and functions dynamically.
Ability to write template rules which respond to user interaction events in the browser.

Extension functions, as listed in the documentation, in the Saxon namespace. The Basic level excludes extension functions that depend on streaming or schema-awareness (saxon:schema(), saxon:stream(), and saxon:validate()); these are included at the Advanced level.

p.i: Some extension functions such as saxon:send-mail are available on the Java platform only.

description.p: Extension functions, as listed in the documentation, in the Saxon namespace. The Basic level excludes extension functions that depend on streaming or schema-awareness.

Extension functions, as listed in the documentation, in the Saxon namespace. The Advanced level includes those that depend on streaming or schema-awareness: saxon:schema(), saxon:stream(), and saxon:validate().
XSLT extension functions and instructions providing access to SQL databases.
Ability to implement XSLT extension instructions by implementing a Saxon-defined interface and registering the implementation with the Saxon Configuration.

At the Basic level, English is the only language supported for formatting numbers as words "out of the box". A further set of installable numberers are available to provide support for some other European languages: Danish (da), German (de), French (fr), Belgium French (fr-BE), Italian (it), Dutch (nl), Belgium Flemish (nl-BE), and Swedish (sv).
At the Advanced level, full support for formatting numbers as words in different languages is provided using the ICU4J library.
At the Basic level, English is the only language supported for formatting dates as words.
At the Advanced level, full support for formatting dates as words in different languages is provided using the ICU library for the relevant platform (ICU4J for SaxonJ and SaxonC, ICU4N for SaxonCS).

alt-description.p: At the Advanced level, full support for formatting dates as words in different languages is provided using the ICU4J library.
At the Advanced level, full support for formatting dates as words in different languages is provided using the ICU4N library.

description.p: At the Basic level, support for sorting and comparison of strings using the Unicode Collation Algorithm uses the collation facilities available directly from the JDK.

At the Advanced level, support for sorting and comparison of strings using the Unicode Collation Algorithm uses the collation facilities available from the ICU library for the relevant platform for Saxon 11 products (ICU4J for SaxonJ and SaxonC, ICU4N for SaxonCS), and using the Intl.Collator JavaScript API for SaxonJS.

alt-description.p: At the Advanced level, support for sorting and comparison of strings using the Unicode Collation Algorithm uses the collation facilities available from the ICU4J library.
At the Advanced level, support for sorting and comparison of strings using the Unicode Collation Algorithm uses the collation facilities available from the ICU4N library.
At the Advanced level, support for sorting and comparison of strings using the Unicode Collation Algorithm uses the collation facilities available from the Intl.Collator JavaScript API.

description.p: SaxonJ's native interface for processing XSLT, XQuery, XPath, and XML Schema, on Java.
SaxonCS's interface for processing XSLT, XQuery, XPath, and XML Schema, on .NET.
SaxonC's interface for processing XSLT, XQuery, XPath, and XML Schema, on C++.
Implementations of the standard JAXP interfaces for XSLT transformation, XPath evaluation, and XML Schema validation.

Implementations of the standard XQJ interfaces for XQuery processing. Note that the XQJ interfaces have been removed from the standard download of Saxon-HE because the Oracle specification license is not open source, but they are available on request.
Interface module that allows SaxonC to be invoked from PHP applications.
Interface module that allows SaxonC to be invoked from Python applications.
Ability to use a DOM (Document Object Model) for the input and output of transformations and queries. On the .NET platform this includes the System.Xml DOM classes.

alt-description.p: Ability to use a DOM (Document Object Model) for the input and output of transformations and queries.
Ability to use a DOM (Document Object Model) for the input and output of transformations.

description.p: Indexing of a supplied DOM tree to provide fast navigation (the Domino Model).

feature.shortName: Support for JDOM2, AXIOM, DOM4J, and XOM

description.p: Ability to use a JDOM2, AXIOM, DOM4J, and XOM for the input or output of transformations and queries. Note that the code for these interfaces is open source and can be compiled to work with Saxon-HE, but it does not come packaged with the Saxon-HE download.

Although the code for these interfaces does not come packaged with the Saxon-HE download, it is open source and can be compiled to work with Saxon-HE. This provides the ability to use a JDOM2, AXIOM, DOM4J, and XOM for the input or output of transformations and queries.
